## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Agent details

Written with Claude Code: the analysis, measurements and test plan below.

**TLDR:** `materialize_mla_kv`, the k/v build shared by DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi K3 MLA, becomes the `mla_kv` local-compile region, which fuses the eager concat kernels. Two DeepSeek-V3 layers at 16k: -2.6% wall, -2.7% under CUDA graphs, -1.07 GB peak (2 layers, no activation remat). Outputs are bitwise; grads are bitwise except k_shared's, a sum over heads in Inductor's order (1 bf16 ulp on 1 of 1,048,576 elements under some configs). `UlyssesMLAAttention` now all-gathers k_shared synchronously, so the region keeps k_shared's grad.

```text
main:     kv -> split -> k_nope, v (a view of kv);  k = cat(k_nope, k_shared on every head)   eager cat; bwd: eager cat
this PR:  region(kv, k_shared) -> k, v (dense when grad is on)                                Triton copies; bwd: one copy + head sum
```

Independent of the PR below it in the stack (no shared files; applies cleanly on main).

**Problem**
1. **Shared k/v build.** `MLAAttention` builds per-head k and v in `materialize_mla_kv`, from packed `kv` `[T, H, 256]` and the shared key `[T, 64]`.
2. **Eager copies.** It splits kv into k_nope and v, broadcasts the shared key to all heads, and concatenates `k = [k_nope, k_shared]` `[T, H, 192]`.
3. **Slow kernels.** Both concats run ATen's generic cat kernel: k's 1552 us vs 189 us at full memory bandwidth (8x), the backward's 1940 vs 302 us (6.4x).
4. **Cost.** 3.55 ms per DeepSeek-V3 layer at 16k, fwd+bwd kernel time (ideal 0.53 ms).

**Solution**
1. **Region.** `materialize_mla_kv` is now the `mla_kv` region. Inductor fuses split, broadcast and concat into one copy kernel, and the backward concat into another.
2. **Dense v when grad is on.** Attention saves v, and a v that views kv keeps all of kv alive. A dense v lets kv go after the forward: -0.54 GB per MLA layer at 16k without activation remat. Under compile the copy is free: it replaces the backward's copy of v's grad.
3. **Ulysses CP.** `UlyssesMLAAttention` all-gathered k_shared with `async_op=True`. A compiled region detaches an unwaited async input, so k_shared's grad came out all zeros under `mla_kv`. The all-gather is now synchronous. The gathered k_shared is `[T, 64]` (2 MB at 16k in bf16); the overlap it loses was not measured.
4. **Enabled** in `DeepSeekV3Model.Config` (Kimi K2.x inherits it) and `KimiK3Model.Config`.
5. **Unchanged:** the function's signature and how both callers call it (`MLAAttention.forward`, also used after the CP all-gather, and `UlyssesMLAAttention.forward`). `no_grad` keeps the view.

**Results**
```text
Numerics: bitwise except one grad. Outputs, k, v and kv's grad are copies: bitwise vs main under every autotune config.
          k_shared's grad sums over heads in Inductor's order, not ATen's: 1 of 1,048,576 elements is 1 bf16 ulp
          off under some reduction configs (op level, DeepSeek-V3 dims).
          rel L2 vs fp64, k_shared grad:  main 1.656e-3 | this PR 1.656e-3
          DeepSeek-V3, 2 layers:  output and all grads bitwise vs main in every run below
          Kimi K3, 2 layers:      output bitwise; grads 5.6e-3 rel L2 vs main, same as main vs main (its backward is nondeterministic)
          Batch invariant in deterministic mode: full batch vs uneven chunks, k, v and both grads bitwise.

Measured on main of 10-20 + this change. That tree's gate also checked is_compiling(); the compiled path is the same, so these rows hold.
DeepSeek-V3 671B layers 2-3 (dense FFN + MoE at one EP8 rank's shapes, 32 experts), native dims, flex attention,
no activation checkpointing except the remat rows, 1x GB300, ms per 2-layer step;
median of 5 fresh processes (16k train), else 1 process
mode                     T     main      this PR  delta
train fwd+bwd            16k   177.48    172.89   -2.6%
train CUDA graphs        16k   176.96    172.22   -2.7%
train fwd+bwd            4k     41.05     39.60   -3.5%
train CUDA graphs        4k     39.36     38.32   -2.6%
train, activation remat  16k   194.82    188.01   -3.5%   (DefaultActivationRematConfig, the 671B recipe's)
prefill no_grad          16k    51.02     48.85   -4.3%
peak memory              16k    34.20     33.13 GB
peak memory, remat       16k    30.38     29.84 GB         (kv is kept for the replay, so the saving is transient)
train 32k: not run (the region's copies are per token, so the 16k delta should scale)

Kimi K3 layers 50 (KDA + MoE) + 51 (MLA + MoE), one EP8 rank's experts, varlen, no AC, 16k, median of 3 processes
train fwd+bwd            16k   215.35    213.25   -0.7%   (median of per-process deltas)
train CUDA graphs        16k   214.47    211.98   -1.2%   (2 processes)
peak memory              16k    73.89     73.48 GB

k/v build alone, kernel time per MLA layer, 16k, us
DeepSeek-V3 fwd+bwd   3550 -> 737   (ideal 530; 680 with the dense-v copy)
DeepSeek-V3 no_grad   1552 -> 218
Kimi K3 fwd+bwd       2682 -> 617

graphs: mla_kv 3 over T = 2k/4k/8k/16k + no_grad (static T, dynamic T, no_grad), limit 8; cold compile ~+1 s (first call, caches off)
```
Decode: not reached in the RL generator, which runs vLLM's native MLA. The exception is batch-invariant mode, whose only MLA configs (the Kimi K3 RL tests) set regions `[]`.

You may ask: why a dense v in eager too? Same memory reason, one code path instead of an eager/compiled fork. Measured 10-19 on the same split + copy, before it moved into `materialize_mla_kv` (2 DeepSeek-V3 layers at 4k): eager +0.2-0.3%, GraphTrainer +0.3-0.8% kernel time.
You may ask: why not a dense v under `no_grad`? Nothing is saved for backward, so it's only a copy: +0.44 ms wall on the 16k prefill (2 layers; two 155 us clones).
You may ask: why not always the view? Same time without activation checkpointing, but +0.54 GB per MLA layer at 16k without activation remat. Under activation remat the forward copy replays: +0.16 ms per layer (0.2%).
NOTE: the region is on in the recipes that keep the model's default regions: `deepseek_v3_671b`, `deepseek_v3_671b_dist_moe_bf16`, `deepseek_v3_671b_dist_moe_mxfp8`, the Kimi K2.x / K3 model configs (debugmodel test recipes), and `rl_grpo_deepseek_v3_debug` (the H100 RL integration test, 4 GPUs: its trainer runs the region, its generator runs vLLM's native MLA). That RL test is the PR's only GPU end-to-end coverage.
NOTE: the region is off in `deepseek_v3_671b_nvfp4_ffn_mxfp8_attn` (regions `["loss"]`), GraphTrainer and SPMD-typechecking configs (regions `[]`), the Kimi K3 RL test configs (`[]`) and the `fused_mla` override (it skips `materialize_mla_kv`). With grad on, these still return a dense v (cost in "You may ask").
NOTE: Ulysses CP: q keeps the packed q/kv buffer alive, so there a dense v adds `[T, H/cp, 128]` per MLA layer instead of saving memory. No recipe uses Ulysses MLA.
NOTE: goldens: the fake-PG A10G DeepSeek-V3 golden is unchanged (bitwise; the region is on there). The real-PG CP+PP goldens (A10G, mi350x) get refreshed if they move. The Kimi K3 B200 golden runs with typechecking, so regions are off there.
NOTE: not tested: varlen DeepSeek-V3 (the 671B recipe's default backend; the region doesn't touch attention), multi-GPU TP and CP, loss curve.

**Test plan**
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py`: 3 passed.
  - region vs eager for the projected and Ulysses input layouts, v dense with grad on. Fails before: eager v is a view, and `mla_kv` is not a region.
  - `UlyssesMLAAttention.forward` on a 1-rank gloo CP group (an SDPA stand-in for FlexInnerAttention, whose compiled flex doesn't build on every CPU): every input and weight grad under `mla_kv` matches eager. Fails without the `cp_mla.py` change: k_shared's grad is all zeros.
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_remat.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_cp_attention.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/deepseek_v3/ tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/kimi_k3/`: 96 passed.
- Core CPU (`tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common`, `muse_spark`, `kimi_k3`, `deepseek_v3`, `recipes`): 497 passed, 3 failed (main's 3). RL CPU: 504 passed, 1 failed (main's `alphabet_sort`).

On the 1-rank gloo group: the all-to-all with `async_op=True` returns a plain `Tensor`, and the k_shared all-gather returns an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`. So the test covers both paths as they run at CP > 1, and q / kv reach `mla_kv` as plain tensors.

**Approve**: the TODO is in, and the all-to-all question is answered. No new problems. See the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5564#pullrequestreview). A maintainer still needs to review.

**Verdict: Approve** -- a small change that follows the existing `local_compile` pattern (`mla_qk`), with measured end-to-end wins and bitwise outputs. A maintainer still needs to review because it touches `models/common/`.

**What this PR does.** It decorates `materialize_mla_kv` (shared by DeepSeek-V3, the Kimi K2.x models that inherit its config, and Kimi K3, including both CP variants) as the `mla_kv` local-compile region, and enables that region in both model configs. It also makes `v` dense when grad is on, so attention no longer saves a view that keeps the whole `[T, H, N+V]` `kv` alive.

**Example.** One DeepSeek-V3 MLA layer at T=16k, grad on:
```text
before: k_nope, v = split(kv)            # v is a view of kv
        k = cat(k_nope, expand(k_shared)) # eager CatArrayBatchedCopy
        attention saves v -> kv [T,H,256] stays alive until backward
after:  one Inductor copy builds k and a dense v
        attention saves the dense v -> kv freed after forward (-0.54 GB/layer)
        no_grad: v is still a view (nothing is saved, so no copy)
```

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py:50` -- the `no_grad` view assertion pins a perf choice and costs a third CPU compile; consider keeping only the grad-on contiguity assert (inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Call sites: `MLAAttention.forward` binds `materialize_kv=materialize_mla_kv` at def time. That binding is the `local_compile` wrapper, so the region applies to `MLAAttention`, to the all-gather CP variant (which calls `MLAAttention.forward`), and to `UlyssesMLAAttention`. The `fused_mla` override passes its own `materialize_kv`, so it isn't affected, as the description says.
- `torch.is_grad_enabled()` inside the region is guarded by Dynamo. That matches the description's 3 graphs (static T, dynamic T, no_grad), which fits under the recompile limit.
- Remat: `recompute_needs_tensor(kv_THP, k_shared_TR)` already keeps `kv` for replay, so with remat on, the dense `v` changes time (the description measures +0.16 ms per layer) but not peak memory.
- The test is in the right place (`models/common`, next to the shared function). The Ulysses parametrization adds real coverage: a non-contiguous `kv` taken from a packed q/kv tensor.
- Eager configs (GraphTrainer, RL with regions `[]`) pay the copy of `v` (+0.2-0.8% kernel time) to get the same memory win. I agree with keeping one code path here.

</details>

Not verified: the GPU perf and memory numbers, and the golden-loss impact on A10G/mi350x (integration runs are still queued). The CPU Unit Test workflow was skipped on this stacked PR, so `test_mla_compile.py` has not run in CI yet.

Optional: the grad-on `v.is_contiguous()` check guards a real memory invariant (a view would keep all of `kv` alive). The `no_grad` check only pins a perf choice (skip a copy nobody saves), and under `["mla_kv"]` it adds a third Inductor compile per parametrization on the CPU runner. Consider dropping these two lines and keeping only the grad-on assert.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the item below before merging** -- the new commit fixes a real silent zero-grad under Ulysses CP with the smallest change and adds a test that fails without it. The workaround still needs a TODO that links an upstream issue. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches `models/common/`.

**What changed since the last review.** `UlyssesMLAAttention` now all-gathers `k_shared` synchronously (`cp_mla.py:107-117`). `test_cp_attention.py` now pins `[False, True, True]` for the async flags. `test_ulysses_mla_grads_match_eager` runs the real forward on a 1-rank gloo group and compares every grad under `mla_kv` against eager. The earlier optional note about the `no_grad` view assert is settled by the author's reply: only that assert catches an always-dense `v`.

**Example.** Ulysses CP with `mla_kv` on, before this commit:
```text
k_shared = redistribute(k_shared, S(0) -> R, async_op=True)  # AsyncCollectiveTensor, not waited
k, v = materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, k_shared)                   # compiled region gets the unwaited input
                                                             # -> detached, k_shared.grad == 0, no error
after:  sync all-gather -> plain tensor -> grad flows; matches eager
```

### Must fix
- `torchtitan/models/common/attention/cp_mla.py:105` -- the comment describes a PyTorch bug: compile silently detaches an unwaited `AsyncCollectiveTensor` input. Add a `TODO` with an upstream issue link so `async_op=True` can come back once it's fixed (see the inline comment).

### Questions
- Under real multi-rank Ulysses, `kv_THP` comes from `torch.split` of the `async_op=True` all-to-all output (`cp_mla.py:121-136`). An `AsyncCollectiveTensor` passes view ops through without waiting, so `kv_THP` may also reach `mla_kv` unwaited. The 1-rank test shows `kv_c.grad` matching eager. Can you confirm that the 1-rank all-to-all really returns an async tensor (and not a short-circuit), so the test covers this path too? If it doesn't, `kv`'s grad may have the same silent zero at CP > 1. *Unverified: I couldn't read the installed `spmd_types` here.*

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Root cause and layer: the fix belongs at the call site because `local_compile` has no place to wait on inputs generically. Waiting in its `wrapped` would also be possible, but `ACT.wait()` returns the inner `elem`, which would drop autograd too, so that isn't a drop-in. The real fix is upstream, hence the TODO.
- Overlap loss: the gathered `k_shared` is `[T, 64]` (about 2 MB at 16k). The all-gather used to overlap with `project_mla_kv` and the packed cat. No recipe uses Ulysses MLA, so the unmeasured cost is acceptable.
- Test placement and cost: `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/` mirrors the source tree. The gloo `HashStore` single-rank group is cheap and guards a silent-grad regression that no other test covers.

</details>

Not verified: GPU perf and memory numbers, and the real-PG CP+PP golden impact.

This works around a PyTorch gap: `torch.compile` takes an unwaited `AsyncCollectiveTensor` input and silently detaches it, so the grad comes out as zeros with no error. The repo rule for upstream workarounds is a `TODO` with an issue link. Without one, nobody will know to restore `async_op=True` once it's fixed. The same silent zero-grad can hit any `local_compile` region that gets an async collective output as a direct input, so filing it upstream is worth more than this one call site.

```suggestion
        # TODO(<issue link>): not async -- torch.compile detaches an unwaited
        # AsyncCollectiveTensor input, so the mla_kv region would drop k_shared's grad.
```

**Verdict: Approve** -- both items from the last review are settled, and the new commit only changes a comment. This touches `models/common/`, so a maintainer still needs to review.

**What changed since the last review.** a5f3fb77b adds `TODO(pytorch/pytorch#191113)` to the synchronous k_shared all-gather (`cp_mla.py:105-106`). No code changed.

**Example.** The Ulysses CP path at HEAD:
```text
k_shared = redistribute(S(0) -> R)                  # synchronous: plain tensor, grad flows
packed   = redistribute(S(0) -> S(1), async_op=True) # spmd_types all-to-all blocks anyway -> plain tensor
q, kv    = split(packed)
k, v     = materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, k_shared)      # mla_kv region: all three inputs keep autograd
```

### Earlier items
- Must fix (TODO with upstream link): resolved. #191113 is a closed, unmerged PR, not an open issue, but it describes this exact bug and gives a future reader the trail to restoring `async_op=True`.
- Question (does `kv_THP` reach `mla_kv` unwaited at CP > 1?): answered. The author says spmd_types' shard all-to-all is a blocking `dist.all_to_all` plus `torch.cat` at every world size and never returns an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`, so `q`/`kv` reach the region as plain tensors. `test_ulysses_mla_grads_match_eager` compares `kv_c.grad` against eager. If spmd_types ever makes the all-to-all truly async, that test fails instead of `kv`'s grad going silently to zero.

No new problems found.

Not verified: the spmd_types internals behind the all-to-all answer (the package isn't readable in this checkout), the GPU perf and memory numbers, and the real-PG CP+PP golden impact.

## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Agent details

Written with Claude Code: the analysis, measurements and test plan below.

**TLDR:** `materialize_mla_kv`, the k/v build shared by DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi K3 MLA, becomes the `mla_kv` local-compile region, which fuses the eager concat kernels. Two DeepSeek-V3 layers at 16k: -2.6% wall, -2.7% under CUDA graphs, -1.07 GB peak (2 layers, no activation remat). Outputs are bitwise; grads are bitwise except k_shared's, a sum over heads in Inductor's order (1 bf16 ulp on 1 of 1,048,576 elements under some configs). `UlyssesMLAAttention` now all-gathers k_shared synchronously, so the region keeps k_shared's grad.

```text
main:     kv -> split -> k_nope, v (a view of kv);  k = cat(k_nope, k_shared on every head)   eager cat; bwd: eager cat
this PR:  region(kv, k_shared) -> k, v (dense when grad is on)                                Triton copies; bwd: one copy + head sum
```

Independent of the PR below it in the stack (no shared files; applies cleanly on main).

**Problem**
1. **Shared k/v build.** `MLAAttention` builds per-head k and v in `materialize_mla_kv`, from packed `kv` `[T, H, 256]` and the shared key `[T, 64]`.
2. **Eager copies.** It splits kv into k_nope and v, broadcasts the shared key to all heads, and concatenates `k = [k_nope, k_shared]` `[T, H, 192]`.
3. **Slow kernels.** Both concats run ATen's generic cat kernel: k's 1552 us vs 189 us at full memory bandwidth (8x), the backward's 1940 vs 302 us (6.4x).
4. **Cost.** 3.55 ms per DeepSeek-V3 layer at 16k, fwd+bwd kernel time (ideal 0.53 ms).

**Solution**
1. **Region.** `materialize_mla_kv` is now the `mla_kv` region. Inductor fuses split, broadcast and concat into one copy kernel, and the backward concat into another.
2. **Dense v when grad is on.** Attention saves v, and a v that views kv keeps all of kv alive. A dense v lets kv go after the forward: -0.54 GB per MLA layer at 16k without activation remat. Under compile the copy is free: it replaces the backward's copy of v's grad.
3. **Ulysses CP.** `UlyssesMLAAttention` all-gathered k_shared with `async_op=True`. A compiled region detaches an unwaited async input, so k_shared's grad came out all zeros under `mla_kv`. The all-gather is now synchronous. The gathered k_shared is `[T, 64]` (2 MB at 16k in bf16); the overlap it loses was not measured.
4. **Enabled** in `DeepSeekV3Model.Config` (Kimi K2.x inherits it) and `KimiK3Model.Config`.
5. **Unchanged:** the function's signature and how both callers call it (`MLAAttention.forward`, also used after the CP all-gather, and `UlyssesMLAAttention.forward`). `no_grad` keeps the view.

**Results**
```text
Numerics: bitwise except one grad. Outputs, k, v and kv's grad are copies: bitwise vs main under every autotune config.
          k_shared's grad sums over heads in Inductor's order, not ATen's: 1 of 1,048,576 elements is 1 bf16 ulp
          off under some reduction configs (op level, DeepSeek-V3 dims).
          rel L2 vs fp64, k_shared grad:  main 1.656e-3 | this PR 1.656e-3
          DeepSeek-V3, 2 layers:  output and all grads bitwise vs main in every run below
          Kimi K3, 2 layers:      output bitwise; grads 5.6e-3 rel L2 vs main, same as main vs main (its backward is nondeterministic)
          Batch invariant in deterministic mode: full batch vs uneven chunks, k, v and both grads bitwise.

Measured on main of 10-20 + this change. That tree's gate also checked is_compiling(); the compiled path is the same, so these rows hold.
DeepSeek-V3 671B layers 2-3 (dense FFN + MoE at one EP8 rank's shapes, 32 experts), native dims, flex attention,
no activation checkpointing except the remat rows, 1x GB300, ms per 2-layer step;
median of 5 fresh processes (16k train), else 1 process

train CUDA graphs        16k   176.96    172.22   -2.7%

train CUDA graphs        4k     39.36     38.32   -2.6%
```

Decode: not reached in the RL generator, which runs vLLM's native MLA. The exception is batch-invariant mode, whose only MLA configs (the Kimi K3 RL tests) set regions `[]`.

You may ask: why a dense v in eager too? Same memory reason, one code path instead of an eager/compiled fork. Measured 10-19 on the same split + copy, before it moved into `materialize_mla_kv` (2 DeepSeek-V3 layers at 4k): eager +0.2-0.3%, GraphTrainer +0.3-0.8% kernel time.
You may ask: why not a dense v under `no_grad`? Nothing is saved for backward, so it's only a copy: +0.44 ms wall on the 16k prefill (2 layers; two 155 us clones).
You may ask: why not always the view? Same time without activation checkpointing, but +0.54 GB per MLA layer at 16k without activation remat. Under activation remat the forward copy replays: +0.16 ms per layer (0.2%).
NOTE: the region is on in the recipes that keep the model's default regions: `deepseek_v3_671b`, `deepseek_v3_671b_dist_moe_bf16`, `deepseek_v3_671b_dist_moe_mxfp8`, the Kimi K2.x / K3 model configs (debugmodel test recipes), and `rl_grpo_deepseek_v3_debug` (the H100 RL integration test, 4 GPUs: its trainer runs the region, its generator runs vLLM's native MLA). That RL test is the PR's only GPU end-to-end coverage.
NOTE: the region is off in `deepseek_v3_671b_nvfp4_ffn_mxfp8_attn` (regions `["loss"]`), GraphTrainer and SPMD-typechecking configs (regions `[]`), the Kimi K3 RL test configs (`[]`) and the `fused_mla` override (it skips `materialize_mla_kv`). With grad on, these still return a dense v (cost in "You may ask").
NOTE: Ulysses CP: q keeps the packed q/kv buffer alive, so there a dense v adds `[T, H/cp, 128]` per MLA layer instead of saving memory. No recipe uses Ulysses MLA.
NOTE: goldens: the fake-PG A10G DeepSeek-V3 golden is unchanged (bitwise; the region is on there). The real-PG CP+PP goldens (A10G, mi350x) get refreshed if they move. The Kimi K3 B200 golden runs with typechecking, so regions are off there.
NOTE: not tested: varlen DeepSeek-V3 (the 671B recipe's default backend; the region doesn't touch attention), multi-GPU TP and CP, loss curve.

**Test plan**
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py`: 3 passed.
  - region vs eager for the projected and Ulysses input layouts, v dense with grad on. Fails before: eager v is a view, and `mla_kv` is not a region.
  - `UlyssesMLAAttention.forward` on a 1-rank gloo CP group (an SDPA stand-in for FlexInnerAttention, whose compiled flex doesn't build on every CPU): every input and weight grad under `mla_kv` matches eager. Fails without the `cp_mla.py` change: k_shared's grad is all zeros.
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_remat.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_cp_attention.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/deepseek_v3/ tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/kimi_k3/`: 96 passed.

+import pytest
+import spmd_types as spmd
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from torchtitan.distributed.local_compile import LocalCompileConfig
+from torchtitan.models.common.attention import (
+    cp_mla,
+    FlexInnerAttention,
+    materialize_mla_kv,
+)
+from torchtitan.models.common.linear import Linear
+
+# T tokens, H heads, N per-head key dims, R shared key dims, V value dims, L latent dims
+T, H, N, R, V, L = 16, 4, 8, 4, 6, 8
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def reset_local_compile():
+    LocalCompileConfig().apply()
+    torch._dynamo.reset()
+    yield
+    LocalCompileConfig().apply()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["projected", "ulysses"])
+def test_compiled_mla_kv_matches_eager(layout: str) -> None:
+    """``projected``: kv viewed from the wkv_b output (MLAAttention).
+    ``ulysses``: q and kv split from one packed tensor (UlyssesMLAAttention)."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    if layout == "projected":
+        bases = [torch.randn(T, H, N + R), torch.randn(T, H * (N + V))]
+    else:
+        bases = [torch.randn(T, H, N + R + N + V)]
+    k_shared = torch.randn(T, R)
+    grad_k, grad_v = torch.randn(T, H, N + R), torch.randn(T, H, V)
+
+    results = []
+    for regions in ([], ["mla_kv"]):
+        LocalCompileConfig(regions=regions).apply()
+        leaves = [t.clone().requires_grad_() for t in (*bases, k_shared)]
+        if layout == "projected":
+            q, kv = leaves[0], leaves[1].view(T, H, N + V)
+        else:
+            q, kv = leaves[0].split([N + R, N + V], dim=-1)
+        k, v = materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, leaves[-1])
+        torch.autograd.backward((k, v), (grad_k, grad_v))
+        results.append((k, v, *(t.grad for t in leaves)))
+
+        assert v.is_contiguous()  # attention saves v; a view would keep kv alive
+        with torch.no_grad():  # nothing is saved, so v stays a view
+            assert not materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, leaves[-1])[1].is_contiguous()
+
+    for eager, compiled in zip(*results, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(compiled, eager)
+
+
+class _CausalSDPA(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Stands in for FlexInnerAttention, whose compiled flex kernel doesn't build on every CPU."""
+
+    def forward(self, q, k, v, **kwargs):
+        q, k, v = (t.transpose(0, 1) for t in (q, k, v))
+        out = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
+        return out.transpose(0, 1)
+
+
+def test_ulysses_mla_grads_match_eager() -> None:
+    """UlyssesMLAAttention on a 1-rank gloo CP group: every grad under ``mla_kv``
+    matches eager. An async k_shared all-gather reaches the region unwaited and
+    detached, so k_shared's grad would be zero."""
+    dist.init_process_group("gloo", store=dist.HashStore(), rank=0, world_size=1)
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        attention = cp_mla.UlyssesMLAAttention.Config(
+            wkv_b=Linear.Config(in_features=L, out_features=H * (N + V)),
+            packed_kv_head_dim=N + V,
+            inner_attention=FlexInnerAttention.Config(),
+        ).build()
+        attention.inner_attention = _CausalSDPA()
+        inputs = (torch.randn(T, H, N + R), torch.randn(T, L), torch.randn(T, R))
+        results = []
+        with (
+            patch.object(cp_mla, "spmd_mesh_group", return_value=dist.group.WORLD),
+            spmd.no_typecheck(),
+        ):
+            for regions in ([], ["mla_kv"]):
+                LocalCompileConfig(regions=regions).apply()
+                attention.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+                q, kv_c, k_shared = (x.clone().requires_grad_() for x in inputs)
+                out = attention(q, kv_c, k_shared, attention_metadata=None)
+                out.backward(torch.ones_like(out))
+                results.append(
+                    (out, q.grad, kv_c.grad, k_shared.grad, attention.wkv_b.weight.grad)
+                )
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+    for eager, compiled in zip(*results, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(compiled, eager)

inline_comments.body:
This works around a PyTorch gap: `torch.compile` takes an unwaited `AsyncCollectiveTensor` input and silently detaches it, so the grad comes out as zeros with no error. The repo rule for upstream workarounds is a `TODO` with an issue link. Without one, nobody will know to restore `async_op=True` once it's fixed. The same silent zero-grad can hit any `local_compile` region that gets an async collective output as a direct input, so filing it upstream is worth more than this one call site.

```suggestion
        # TODO(<issue link>): not async -- torch.compile detaches an unwaited
        # AsyncCollectiveTensor input, so the mla_kv region would drop k_shared's grad.
```

**Verdict: Approve** -- a small change that follows the existing `local_compile` pattern (`mla_qk`), with measured end-to-end wins and bitwise outputs. A maintainer still needs to review because it touches `models/common/`.

**What this PR does.** It decorates `materialize_mla_kv` (shared by DeepSeek-V3, the Kimi K2.x models that inherit its config, and Kimi K3, including both CP variants) as the `mla_kv` local-compile region, and enables that region in both model configs. It also makes `v` dense when grad is on, so attention no longer saves a view that keeps the whole `[T, H, N+V]` `kv` alive.

**Example.** One DeepSeek-V3 MLA layer at T=16k, grad on:
```text
before: k_nope, v = split(kv)            # v is a view of kv
        k = cat(k_nope, expand(k_shared)) # eager CatArrayBatchedCopy
        attention saves v -> kv [T,H,256] stays alive until backward
after:  one Inductor copy builds k and a dense v
        attention saves the dense v -> kv freed after forward (-0.54 GB/layer)
        no_grad: v is still a view (nothing is saved, so no copy)
```

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_mla_compile.py:50` -- the `no_grad` view assertion pins a perf choice and costs a third CPU compile; consider keeping only the grad-on contiguity assert (inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Call sites: `MLAAttention.forward` binds `materialize_kv=materialize_mla_kv` at def time. That binding is the `local_compile` wrapper, so the region applies to `MLAAttention`, to the all-gather CP variant (which calls `MLAAttention.forward`), and to `UlyssesMLAAttention`. The `fused_mla` override passes its own `materialize_kv`, so it isn't affected, as the description says.
- `torch.is_grad_enabled()` inside the region is guarded by Dynamo. That matches the description's 3 graphs (static T, dynamic T, no_grad), which fits under the recompile limit.
- Remat: `recompute_needs_tensor(kv_THP, k_shared_TR)` already keeps `kv` for replay, so with remat on, the dense `v` changes time (the description measures +0.16 ms per layer) but not peak memory.
- The test is in the right place (`models/common`, next to the shared function). The Ulysses parametrization adds real coverage: a non-contiguous `kv` taken from a packed q/kv tensor.
- Eager configs (GraphTrainer, RL with regions `[]`) pay the copy of `v` (+0.2-0.8% kernel time) to get the same memory win. I agree with keeping one code path here.

</details>

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the item below before merging** -- the new commit fixes a real silent zero-grad under Ulysses CP with the smallest change and adds a test that fails without it. The workaround still needs a TODO that links an upstream issue. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches `models/common/`.

**What changed since the last review.** `UlyssesMLAAttention` now all-gathers `k_shared` synchronously (`cp_mla.py:107-117`). `test_cp_attention.py` now pins `[False, True, True]` for the async flags. `test_ulysses_mla_grads_match_eager` runs the real forward on a 1-rank gloo group and compares every grad under `mla_kv` against eager. The earlier optional note about the `no_grad` view assert is settled by the author's reply: only that assert catches an always-dense `v`.

**Example.** Ulysses CP with `mla_kv` on, before this commit:
```text
k_shared = redistribute(k_shared, S(0) -> R, async_op=True)  # AsyncCollectiveTensor, not waited
k, v = materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, k_shared)                   # compiled region gets the unwaited input
                                                             # -> detached, k_shared.grad == 0, no error
after:  sync all-gather -> plain tensor -> grad flows; matches eager
```

### Must fix
- `torchtitan/models/common/attention/cp_mla.py:105` -- the comment describes a PyTorch bug: compile silently detaches an unwaited `AsyncCollectiveTensor` input. Add a `TODO` with an upstream issue link so `async_op=True` can come back once it's fixed (see the inline comment).

### Questions
- Under real multi-rank Ulysses, `kv_THP` comes from `torch.split` of the `async_op=True` all-to-all output (`cp_mla.py:121-136`). An `AsyncCollectiveTensor` passes view ops through without waiting, so `kv_THP` may also reach `mla_kv` unwaited. The 1-rank test shows `kv_c.grad` matching eager. Can you confirm that the 1-rank all-to-all really returns an async tensor (and not a short-circuit), so the test covers this path too? If it doesn't, `kv`'s grad may have the same silent zero at CP > 1. *Unverified: I couldn't read the installed `spmd_types` here.*

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Root cause and layer: the fix belongs at the call site because `local_compile` has no place to wait on inputs generically. Waiting in its `wrapped` would also be possible, but `ACT.wait()` returns the inner `elem`, which would drop autograd too, so that isn't a drop-in. The real fix is upstream, hence the TODO.
- Overlap loss: the gathered `k_shared` is `[T, 64]` (about 2 MB at 16k). The all-gather used to overlap with `project_mla_kv` and the packed cat. No recipe uses Ulysses MLA, so the unmeasured cost is acceptable.
- Test placement and cost: `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/` mirrors the source tree. The gloo `HashStore` single-rank group is cheap and guards a silent-grad regression that no other test covers.

</details>

Not verified: GPU perf and memory numbers, and the real-PG CP+PP golden impact.

**Verdict: Approve** -- both items from the last review are settled, and the new commit only changes a comment. This touches `models/common/`, so a maintainer still needs to review.

**What changed since the last review.** a5f3fb77b adds `TODO(pytorch/pytorch#191113)` to the synchronous k_shared all-gather (`cp_mla.py:105-106`). No code changed.

**Example.** The Ulysses CP path at HEAD:
```text
k_shared = redistribute(S(0) -> R)                  # synchronous: plain tensor, grad flows
packed   = redistribute(S(0) -> S(1), async_op=True) # spmd_types all-to-all blocks anyway -> plain tensor
q, kv    = split(packed)
k, v     = materialize_mla_kv(q, kv, k_shared)      # mla_kv region: all three inputs keep autograd
```

### Earlier items
- Must fix (TODO with upstream link): resolved. #191113 is a closed, unmerged PR, not an open issue, but it describes this exact bug and gives a future reader the trail to restoring `async_op=True`.
- Question (does `kv_THP` reach `mla_kv` unwaited at CP > 1?): answered. The author says spmd_types' shard all-to-all is a blocking `dist.all_to_all` plus `torch.cat` at every world size and never returns an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`, so `q`/`kv` reach the region as plain tensors. `test_ulysses_mla_grads_match_eager` compares `kv_c.grad` against eager. If spmd_types ever makes the all-to-all truly async, that test fails instead of `kv`'s grad going silently to zero.

No new problems found.
